brief: TME's September 10 call that bond volatility (MOVE) was underpriced has played out: MOVE rose from 77 to 113, near the March panic highs, while VIX barely moved, widening the MOVE-VIX spread. Because SPX no longer reacts to macro, GS says traders have shifted macro expression into fixed-income ETF options: FICC ETF option volume has more than doubled in three weeks, with volumes in HYG, LQD, TLT and IEF running toward 2.2-2.4 million contracts on a 10-day average. GS finds SPX's correlation with cross-asset signals has broken down ("the equity market is trading the Fed, the bond market is trading the regime"), and SPX has also decoupled from its own internals: the 52-week high/low breadth spread has collapsed to around -20 even as SPX sits near 7,700, and index-to-sector correlations have fallen. GS's Vol Panic Index stays below 2/10 and the VIX/HYG implied-vol ratio is at a 3+ year low, so GS still likes VIX upside convexity for anyone skeptical. Separately, DB cautions the resulting dovish Fed repricing may not bring a rescue this time: unlike the 2010s, inflation is above target, and in 2022-23 similar dovish repricing (Ukraine, the UK mini-budget, SVB) was each time reversed as persistent inflation forced tightening, so financial stress no longer automatically equals a central-bank rescue.
